reason: The claim asserts universal causal improvement across "all real Internet paths in every region." The candidate is a single-condition emulation on one host with two flows and no treatment contrast. Critical issues: (1) Causal claims require a treatment contrast (e.g., with vs. without the algorithm); the candidate has no such contrast. (2) A single emulated host cannot represent "all real Internet paths in every region" — this is a vast generalization gap. (3) The candidate's own metadata acknowledges "no treatment contrast" and "not scientific evidence." (4) Two co-located flows on one host are not independent samples from diverse network conditions; no sampling or dependence design is present. (5) Emulated netem conditions do not establish behavior on real heterogeneous Internet paths with variable congestion, routing, and infrastructure. (6) No regional diversity is tested. The candidate cannot support the causal, universal scope of the original claim under any reasonable methodology. Coverage is not complete because the claim's scope (all real paths, every region, causal mechanism) is far beyond what this single-host emulation can address.
